# Nehemiah Chapter 4 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 471r–471v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/NEH_004_page_001.jpg

---

**1** When Sanballat found out we were rebuilding the wall, he flew into a rage and ridiculed the Jews.

**2** In front of his allies and the Samaritan army he sneered, "What do these pathetic Jews think they're doing? Do they think they can just rebuild? Will they offer sacrifices? Finish in a single day? Pull living stones from piles of burned rubble?"

**3** Tobiah the Ammonite, standing beside him, added, "Whatever they build, even a fox climbing on it would knock it down!"

**4** We prayed, "Hear us, O God — we are being mocked! Turn their insults back on them. Hand them over to be plundered in a land of exile.

**5** Do not forgive their offenses or let their sins be erased from your sight, for they have insulted you in front of the builders."

**6** So we kept building, and the entire wall was joined together at half its height — because the people were determined to work.

**7** When Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabs, the Ammonites, and the people of Ashdod learned that the repairs to Jerusalem's walls were advancing and that the gaps were being closed, they were furious.

**8** They all plotted together to attack Jerusalem and throw everything into chaos.

**9** But we prayed to our God and posted guards around the clock to defend against them.

**10** Meanwhile, the people of Judah were saying, "The laborers are exhausted, and the rubble is overwhelming. We'll never be able to rebuild this wall."

**11** Our enemies were saying, "Before they know what's happening, we'll appear among them, kill them, and put an end to this project."

**12** Jews living near the enemy came and warned us again and again — ten times — "They will attack from every direction!"

**13** So I positioned armed men at the most vulnerable points behind the wall, in the exposed areas. I organized them by families, armed with swords, spears, and bows.

**14** After surveying the situation, I stood and addressed the nobles, the officials, and all the people: "Don't be afraid of them! Remember the Lord, who is great and awesome. Fight for your families — your brothers, your sons, your daughters, your wives, and your homes!"

**15** When our enemies realized we had discovered their plot and that God had thwarted their plans, we all went back to the wall, each to his section.

**16** From that day forward, I split my workforce: half built while the other half stood guard with spears, shields, bows, and body armor. The officers backed up the entire workforce of Judah.

**17** The wall builders and load carriers worked with a tool in one hand and a weapon in the other.

**18** Every builder wore a sword strapped to his side as he worked. The trumpeter stayed right beside me.

**19** I told the leaders and all the people, "The project is enormous and we're spread thin along the wall, far apart from each other.

**20** When you hear the trumpet blast, rush to that spot. Our God will fight for us!"

**21** So we pressed on with the work from first light until the stars appeared, with half the men standing guard the entire time.

**22** I also ordered everyone to sleep inside Jerusalem with their servants, so they could serve as guards at night and workers during the day.

**23** None of us changed our clothes — not I, not my brothers, not my servants, not my bodyguards. We kept our weapons with us at all times.

---

## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes
1. **Mockery as spiritual warfare** — Sanballat and Tobiah's ridicule (vv. 1-3) is not mere political opposition but an assault on faith itself. Their taunts question whether God's ruined city can ever be restored — the perennial challenge to hope.
2. **The armed builder** — The image of workers with a tool in one hand and a weapon in the other (v. 17) has become one of Scripture's most enduring metaphors for the life of faith: building God's purposes while remaining vigilant against opposition.
3. **"Our God will fight for us"** — Nehemiah's rallying cry (v. 20) echoes the Exodus tradition (cf. Exod 14:14). The trumpet that summons the builders is the same instrument that brought down Jericho's walls — now it defends Jerusalem's.

*— PNEUMA*
